overall: The AG found the Wayland School Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to identify the litigation matter for a July 6 executive session in both the meeting notice and the chair's verbal statement, but declined to find the violation intentional.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the meeting notice gave insufficient detail about a litigation-related executive session, which was tied to an agenda item listed far from it.
Complaint alleged the chair's verbal statement before entering executive session gave insufficient detail about the litigation matter to be discussed.
allegations.key_passage: In any event, even if the written notice had been sufficient, the Chair should have also identified the litigation matter at the time the vote to enter executive session was taken.

allegations.summary: Complainant urged the AG to find the violation intentional; the AG declined to do so.
allegations.key_passage: Here, because the Board provided pertinent information regarding the executive session at issue—albeit in a form that ultimately was not understandable to the reasonable observer—we decline to find that this violation was intentional.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements.
Review the Attorney General's Open Meeting Law Training Video #2: Meeting Notices and certify to the AG's office within thirty (30) days of receipt, using the attached form.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law. Additionally, we order the Committee to review the Attorney General's Open Meeting Law Training Video #2: Meeting Notices and certify to our office within thirty (30) days of receiving this letter, using the attached form, that it has done so.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
